Maya K: Handoff for the 17:00->01:00 UTC window. TL;DR: ingestion backlog + kv-cache evictions + one noisy model node. No active P0s, but two items to watch and one followup for infra.

Maya K: Incident summary:
• embeddings-ingest (eu-west1): ingestion workers started failing with `503` from S3 upstream ~16:30 UTC. Backlog ~12k items. Mitigation: increased batcher replicas, enabled aggressive retry in worker (3 -> 6), and flipped ingestion to fallback region for high-priority customers. Current ingest throughput ~75% of normal.
• kvcache-evictions: observed eviction storm around 16:45 causing transient 429s for SDK v2 clients. We applied temporary TTL bump (evict -> 20m) and adjusted eviction threshold. Metrics: eviction rate down 85%.
• model-serving-alpha: one node in alpha pool reported sustained CPU > 95% for ~10m, autoscaler removed that pod and rolled traffic to beta. No 5xxs from clients.

Maya K: What I did / actions taken:
- Rolled ingestion batchers to larger instance type and restarted the queue processor (cmd: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/ingest-batchers -n eu-west1`).
- Bumped kvcache TTL via `curl` to config service and validated lower eviction metrics.
- Triggered canary shift for alpha -> beta for the model route serving small customers.
- Opened infra ticket to request S3 read concurrency bump and temporary quota for eu-west1 batchers (INC-4567).

Maya K: Current blockers / needs:
- Infra needs to approve the S3 concurrency increase, otherwise fallback region will keep higher latencies for some customers.
- One customer still has ~2k stuck items that need manual retry due to malformed records — I flagged to CS to get clean copy.

Maya K: Next steps for oncoming:
- Monitor ingestion backlog metric `ingest.backlog.count` until <2k.
- Keep an eye on eviction rate `kvcache.evictions.per_min` and client 429s.
- If ingestion throughput doesn't recover to >90% in 30m after infra change, escalate oncall -> infra lead.
- If model-serving node shows recurring CPU >90% after 2 restarts, plan a controlled node replacement and hold canary.

Aj Patel: Thanks Maya. Quick Q — where's the runbook for the ingestion fallback?

Maya K: Runbook link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/ingest-fallback (see section "eu-west1 emergency fallback"). Also pasted the minimal steps: 1) scale batchers 2) enable retry policy 3) flip high-priority routing flag.

Leo Huang: Noted. I'll watch `ingest.backlog.count` for the next hour and pick up escalation if it creeps. I can be paged at +1 if needed.

SRE Bot: Alert: embeddings-ingest eu-west1 S3 errors increased by 420% at 2026-03-17T16:31:02Z. Incident INC-4567 created. PagerDuty notified.

Toni R: For the stuck 2k records, CS is already pulling the payloads from the support ticket. If they clean and re-submit, can we set a temporary `ingest.priority=high` flag for that customer to avoid queue tail latency?

Maya K: Yes we can. Toni, once CS gives the packaged payloads, ping me and I'll kick an expedited requeue with `priority=high`.

Aj Patel: One more — do we want to lift the kvcache eviction threshold permanently or does that risk memory bloat?

Leo Huang: Temp bump is safe short-term. We should run a mem-usage dash probe overnight and revert TTL in the morning if mem climbs. I'll add a dashboard alert `kvcache.memory.percent > 75` for the night.

Maya K: All right. Handing off. Oncall notes: paging policy unchanged, no customer-impacting SLO breaches reported yet. Tagging the oncoming shift: @Aj, @Leo, @Toni. :wave:

Aj Patel: Acknowledged. I'll take the first 30min watch and update in this thread if anything changes. :eyes:

Leo Huang: Got it. Will check dashboards every 15m.

Toni R: Standing by for CS payloads. GL HF. :thumbsup:
